items.title: Louis Tio Interview, 1960-10-26
items.q: Bruce Cochard have a record of it if you ever want to hear him.

ctx.x: How about the Red Man Blues? Did he write that? Red Man Blues? I don't know. I don't know.
Bruce Cochard have a record of it if you ever want to hear him. He played a clarinet and a Red Man.

Yeah. I wouldn't know. I know that he played many a number such as, uh, um, I know he had clarinet solo one time in, uh, I wish, at P. Rowe's number. Um, Sister Kate. I wish I knew what it was. Sister Kate. Well, he, uh, he did a lot of numbers, but I don't know what they were because he was in New York and I was here. Of course, he didn't believe in going around a whole lot of publicity. He knew that, uh, New York had a lot of racket to it. And, uh, he knew that if in case he would get, uh, they'd tell you,…
